WATER SCARCITY 
883 SHRI K.R. SURESH REDDY 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether the level of awareness and sensitivity about judicious and optimum use of water is very 
low among water consumers across various sectors (agricultural, domestic, industrial and commercial; 
(b) whether Government is aware of the emerging water scarcity; 
(c) if so, the steps proposed to be taken by Government keeping in view of the fact that water 
harvesting and conservation are nearly non-existent across these sectors; and 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI BISHWESWAR TUDU) 
(a) Government is continuously trying to increase the level of awareness and sensitivity about 
judicious and optimum use of water among water consumers across various sectors. 
(b)  The average annual water resources potential in the country is assessed as 1999.20 BCM andgiven 
in the CWC report entitled “Reassessment of Water Availability in India using Space Inputs”. The 
increase in population, agricultural and industrial demands resulted in reductionin per capita water 
availability. In 1951, the per capita water availability was 5,177 cubic meter per year (i.e. about 5.18 
million liters per year). On the basis of the population indicated in 2011 census, the per capita water 
availability worked out to about 1545 cubic meter per year (i.e. about 1.55 million liters per year). In 
view of topographical constraints and hydrological features, the utilizable water has been estimated to 
be about 1,122 BCM. 
(690 BCM surface water as assessed by CWC and 432 BCM ground water as assessed by CGWB).The 
per capita average annual water availability in the country is reducing progressively due to increase in 
population.  
(c) & (d) Water being a State subject, steps for augmentation, conservation and effective management 
of water resources are primarily undertaken by the respective State Governments with the technical 
and financial assistance to them through various schemes and programmes of Central Government. 
Various steps taken by the Government for water harvesting and conservation are as below: 
285

I. National Water Policy (2012) advocates promotion, protection and conservation of water. 
II. In rural areas, Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) 
is major scheme driving water harvesting and conservation efforts. 
III. Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) implements Atal Mission for Rejuvenation 
and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) in municipal areas which, inter-alia includes water 
conservation as one of the project component. 
IV. Unified Building Bye Laws (UBBL) of Delhi, 2016, Model Building Bye Laws (MBBL), 2016 
and; Urban and Regional Development Plan Formulation and Implementation (URDPFI) 
Guidelines, 2014 has been formulated with adequate focus on water conservation measures. 
V. Master Plan for Artificial Recharge to Groundwater, 2020 has been prepared by Central Ground 
Water Board with the objective of construction of rain water harvesting structures, thus 
promoting water conservation. 
VI. A Model Bill has been circulated to all the States/ UTs to enable them to enact suitable ground 
water legislation which is aimed at water conservation. So far, 19 States/ UTs have adopted and 
implemented the ground water legislation. 
VII. States/ UTs have been advised to enable Rural Local Bodies (RLBs)/ Panchayats to utilise 15 th 
Fi
nance Commission grants to take up rain water harvesting in Government Buildings like 
panchayats, bhawans, anganwadis, Primary Health Centres etc. 
VIII. Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA) has issued directives to all States/ UTs to take 
measures to promote/ adopt artificial recharge to ground water/ rain water harvesting. Its grants 
permits for use of ground water with mandatory conditions for conservation, augmentation and 
efficient use of ground water. 
IX. Ministry of Jal Shakti has been implementing various schemes/ campaigns for promotion of 
water harvesting and conservation. Jal Shakti Abhiyan-1 was launched in 2019 in 1592 blocks 
out of 2836 blocks in 256 water stressed districts of the country to promote water conservation 
and water resources management. Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch The Rain campaign was launched 
in 2021, in all districts of the country. It had focused interventions i.e. rain water harvesting & 
water conservation among others. Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch The Rain 2022 has been launched 
on 29.03.2022 in all districts of the country. The focused interventions includes water 
conservation and rain water harvesting. Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY).  
X. “Sahi Fasal” campaign was launched by Ministry of Jal Shakti in 2019 focusing on critical and 
over-exploited areas to nudge farmers in the water stressed areas to grow crops which are not 
water intensive, but use water very efficiently; and are economically remunerative; healthy and 
nutritious; environmentally friendly and suited to the agro-climatic-hydro characteristics of the 
area. Series of meetings with farmers were organised in Amritsar, Aurangabad, Kurushetra and 
in New Delhi. 
286

XI. Atal Bhujal Yojana (ABY) has been implemented by the Ministry of Jal Shakti for sustainable 
management of ground water with community participation in the identified over-exploited and 
water stressed areas in the States of Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, 
Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. 
XII. Public Interaction Programs are being organised at grass root level for disseminating the tenets 
under National Aquifer Mapping and Management (NAQUIM) Programme for the benefit of 
the stakeholders. 
XIII. Ministry of Jal Shakti organizes trainings, seminars, workshops, exhibitions, webinars, painting 
competitions etc. to stimulate awareness of stakeholders and encourage people to become 
active participants/ water heroes in water harvesting and conservation. 
XIV. Under the Information, Education and Communication (IEC) scheme, mass awareness 
programmes for water conservation are conducted from time to time each year. Posts on 
awareness on water harvesting and conservation have been shared regularly on the 
Department’s social media platforms like Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, Youtube etc. 
XV. The Ministry has instituted National Water Awards to incentivise good practices done in water 
conservation and management. The first National Water Awards were launched in 2018, the 
second in 2019, the third in 2020. These awards focused on recognizing good work and efforts 
by individuals and organisations across all sectors to create awareness among people about 
importance of water including water harvesting and conservation.

891 SHRI B. LINGAIAH YADAV 
 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of presence of microplastics in rivers harmful for fish and aqua life and loss estimated till 
date since last five years, river wise; and 
(b) the details of various studies done by researchers who are trying to understand how microplastics enter 
the rivers and its affect on others along with corrective steps being taken to avoid such situation in future? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
 
(SHRI BISHWESWAR TUDU) 
(a) & (b)  Rivers, lakes, wetlands and other water bodies in the country are polluted mainly due to 
discharge of untreated or partially treated sewage from cities/towns and industrial effluents in their 
respective catchments, poor operation and maintenance of sewage/effluent treatment plants, lack of 
dilution, dumping of solid waste  on their banks and other non-point sources of pollution. Rapid

(CPCB) in February, 2022 to monitor emerging pollutants (EPs) including micro-plastics in river Ganga on 
annual basis, from its  origin to its  confluence with the Bay of Bengal. 
ICAR-CIFR, Namami Gange and Wildlife Institute of India has conducted several awareness campaigns 
along the riverbanks and in a number of schools on the harmful effect of microplastics in the rivers, and 
importance of proper disposal of single use plastics to minimize the plastic load in aquatic environments. 
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs under the aegis of Swachh Bharat Mission–Urban, has launched 
“Clean Green Campaign” with massive citizen participation for effective management of plastic waste and 
to ensure enforcement of ban on specific single use plastic (SUP) items. As on 1st July, 2022 ,all the 35 
States/Union Territories have notified the SUP ban.

SAFETY OF HIRAKUD DAM IN ODISHA  
894 SHRI SUJEET KUMAR 
 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether dams located within the Mahanadi basin in Chhattisgarh are being operated adhering to any 
Standard Operating Procedure (SOP); and 
(b) whether the State of Chhattisgarh has kept any provision in their reservoirs to absorb flood water 
temporarily in Mahanadi basin for safety of Hirakud dam in Odisha? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
 
(SHRI BISHWESWAR TUDU) 
 
(a) & (b)  Operation and maintenance of dams are carried out by dam owners who are generally State 
Governments, Central and State power generating PSUs, Municipalities and private companies etc. All the 
dam owners are required to have operation & maintenance (O&M) manual containing standard operating 
procedure for their dams/reservoirs in place before commissioning of the dam. CWC has issued guidelines 
for preparation of O&M manual i.e. "Guideline for Preparing Operation and Maintenance Manual for 
Dams" in January 2018. As per the Dam Safety Act 2021 which came in force w.e.f. 30.12.2021, every 
owner of the specified dam shall ensure that a well documented operation and maintenance manual is kept 
at each of the specified dams and are followed at all times.  
  
Dam Safety Act 2021 also provides that every owner of the dam shall make available the information 
relating to maximum anticipated inflows and outflows including flood warning and an adverse impact of 
the same, if any, on persons and property towards the upstream or downstream of the dam, to the 
concerned district authorities and also make available the information in public domain. Dam owners shall 
also have to prepare the emergency action plan of each of their dams which includes inter alia   (i) the type 
of emergencies which are likely to occur in the operation of any reservoir; (ii) identification of the likely 
catastrophic flood in the event of any dam failure, along with probable areas, population, structures and 
installations likely to be adversely affected due to flood water released from the reservoir; (iii) warning 
procedures, inundation maps and advance preparations for handling efficiently the likely adverse situations 
especially to avoid loss of human life.

harvest the runoff water in stream to store at suitable locations for augmenting 
recharge to the ground water in 3 aspirational districts: Osmanabad, 
Maharashtra, YSR Kadapa district, Andhra Pr adesh and Jangaon district, 
Telangana. The structures constructed included check dams, percolation tanks, 
subsurface barrier, recharge wells and recharge shafts. 
• CGWB took up a pilot project in the eastern region of Maharashtra covering 
districts of Wardha  and Amravati at five locations for construction of Bridge 
cum Bandhara (BCB) for ground water recharge. The structures serve the dual 
purposes of transportation as well as storage of water in the upstream side for 
drinking and irrigation needs. The projec t commenced in the year of 2018 and 
was completed in 2020. 
• During 2021-22, CGWB has taken up the project on ‘Groundwater augmentation 
through artificial recharge in identified water stressed areas of Rajasthan, 
comprising Jodhpur, Jaisalmer & Sikar distric ts of Rajasthan. The structures 
include check dams, anicuts and recharge shaft with ponds. So far, Rs. 9.42 Cr. 
has been released by CGWB to WAPCOS for execution.

Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state:

for the past three years, year-wise; 
(b) the amount of funds allocated, disbursed, and utilized for the JSA campaign programmes in Tamil Nadu 
for the past three years, district-wise and the details thereof; and 
(c) whether Government has undertaken a study about the rainwater conserved across various districts in 
Tamil Nadu for the past three years; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
 
(SHRI BISHWESWAR TUDU) 
 
(a) Jal Shakti Abhiyan-I (JSA-I) was conducted in 2019 in 1592 blocks out of 2836 blocks in 256 water stressed 
districts of the country including Tamil Nadu and was expanded as “Jal Shakti Abhiyan:Catch the Rain” (JSA:CTR) in 
2021 with the theme “Catch the Rain - Where it Falls When it Falls” to cover all the blocks of all districts (rural as 
well as urban areas) across the country.  "Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain” (JSA:CTR) -2022 campaign, the third in 
the series of JSAs, has been launched on 29.3.2022 to cover all the blocks of all districts (rural as well as urban areas) 
across the country. 
 
(b) Allocation /disbursement/expenditure under JSA is convergence of various schemes of Central stakeholder 
Ministries/Departments.  State Governments has also been requested to utilise their own resources and also to carry 
out works through locally mobilised funds.  However, funds utlisation under JSA:CTR and JSA:CTR-2022 through 
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS), as uploaded on JSA:CTR portal 
(jsactr.mowr.gov.in) in Tamil Nadu district-wise is enclosed as Annexure-I and Annexure-II respectively. Financial 
grant of Rs. 2.00 lakh is allocated to every district to meet part of the expenditure in GIS mapping of water bodies and 
preparation of scientific plans. Initially, Rs. 1.00 lakh is given  and remaining Rs. 1.00 lakh is given based on the 
performance and quality of work done in this planning process in every district.  Till date Rs. 34.00 lakh have been 
released as 1st instalment in Tamilnadu to Kallakurichi, Nagapattinam, Sivaganga, Tenkasi, Kancheepuram, 
Kanyakumari, Ariyalur, Coimbatore, Cuddalore, Dharmapuri, Dindigul, Karur, Krishnagiri, Perambalur, 
Ramanathapuram, Nilgiris, Theni, Thoothukudi (Tuticorin), Tiruchirappalli, Tirunelveli, Tiruvallur, Tiruvarur, 
Ranipet, Tirupathur, Viluppuram, Virudhunagar, Namakkal, Tiruvannamalai, Erode, Thanjavur, Tiruppur, 
Chengalpattu, Salem, Vellore districts. 
(c) & (d)  No information has been received regarding undertaking a study about the rainwater conserved across 
various districts in Tamil Nadu for the past three years.  However, Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) regularly 
conducts dynamic groundwater resource assessment of the country, including low groundwater areas, in collaboration 
with states. The last groundwater assessment in this regard was made in 2020.  Further, CGWB periodically monitors 
ground water levels throughout the country through a network of monitoring wells.  Groundwater level data of Tamil 
Nadu for the last 3 year i.e. 2019, 2020 and 2021 is attached as Annexure III, IV and V respectively.

STATUS OF JJM IN ANDHRA PRADESH 
 
897.  SHRI MASTHAN RAO BEEDA: 
         SHRI VENKATARAMAN RAO MOPIDEVI 
 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state :- 
(a) the percentage of households in the rural areas in the State of Andhra Pradesh  provided with 
potable tap water supply; 
(b) whether Government will be able t o achieve 100 per cent target under Jal Jeevan  Mission 
(JJM) in the State of Andhra Pradesh; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI PRAHLAD SINGH PATEL) 
 
 
(a) to (c) Since August, 2019, Government of India in partnership with States, is implementing 
Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) – Har Ghar Jal, to make provision of potable tap water supply to every 
rural household in the country by 2024. 
As reported by State Government of Andhr a Pradesh, out of total 95.69 Lakhs rural households 
in the State, 57.47 Lakhs (60.06%) households are provided with  potable tap water supply. As 
per the saturation plan of Andhra Pradesh,  all remaining rural households in the State are 
targeted to be provided with tap water supply by March, 2024. 
To achieve the targeted goal of JJM, a  number of steps have been taken to plan and implement 
JJM in the whole country including  Andhra Pradesh, which, inter alia, includes finalization of 
saturation plan and annua l actionplan (AAP) of respective State/ UT, regular review of 
implementation, workshops/ conferences/webinars for capacity building, trainings, knowledge 
sharing, field visits by multi-disciplinaryteams to provide technical support, etc.  
310

A detailed Operat ional Guidelines for the  implementation of JJM; Margdarshika for Gram 
Panchayats & VWSCs to provide safe drinkingwater in rural households and Guidelines on a 
special campaign to provide piped water supply in schools, anganwadi centres, and ashramshalas 
have been shared with States/ UTs, including  Andhra Pradesh  to facilitate planning and 
implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission. For online  monitoring, JJM –Integrated Management 
Information System (IMIS) and JJM –Dashboard hasbeen put in place. Provision has a lso been 
made for transparent online financial management through Public Financial Management System 
(PFMS). 
 
To expedite the implementation of JJM in Andhra Pradesh, concerted efforts are being made to 
impress upon the State  Government to implement JJM on the ground with speed. Further, 
allocation ofCentral fund to Andhra Pradesh under JJM in 202 2-23, has also been increased to 
Rs. 3,458.20 Crorefrom Rs. 3,182.88 Crore in 2021-22.

SUPPLY OF DRINKING WATER IN ARID DISTRICTS 
898 DR. KANIMOZHI NVN SOMU:  
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state:  
(a) whether Government has chalked out any new scheme to provide drinking water for all 
particularly in arid districts of the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the funds allocated to such schemes during the last three years, year-wise, State-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI PRAHLAD SINGH PATEL)  
 
(a) & (b) Since August 2019, Government of India, in partnership with States, is implementing Jal 
Jeevan Mission (JJM) for making provision of potable tap water supply to eve ry rural household, 
including those in arid and water scarce districts, by 2024. The estimated outlay of the mission is Rs. 
3.60 lakh Crore, out of which Central share is Rs. 2.08 lakh Crore. 
At the time of announcement of Jal Jeevan Mission, 3.23 Crore ho useholds were reported to have 
tap water connections. So far, more than 6.6 1 Crore rural households have been provided with tap 
water connections in last 35 months. Thus, as of date, out of 19.13 Crore rural households in the 
country, 9.84 Crore (51.43%) households are reported to have tap water supply in their homes. 
Under the mission, 30% weightage is assigned for difficult terrains which inter alia include areas 
under Desert Development Programme (DDP) and Drought Prone Area Programme (DPAP) while 
allocating the fund, to prioritize the coverage in these areas . Further, provisions have been made in 
the operational guidelines for planning and implementation of bulk water transfer from long 
distances and regional water supply schemes  for ensuring tap water s upply in drought -prone & 
water-scarce areas/ areas with inadequate rainfall or dependable ground water sources . In addition, 
312

provisions have also been made for source recharging, viz. dedicated bore well recharge structures, 
rain water recharge, rejuvenati on of existing water bodies, etc., in convergence with other schemes 
such as MGNREGS, Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP), 15th Finance 
Commission tied grants to RLBs/ PRIs, State schemes, CSR funds, etc.  
Further, for villages in water -scarce areas, in order to save the precious fresh water, States are also 
being encouraged to plan new water supply scheme with dual piped water supply system, i.e. supply 
of fresh water in one and treated grey/ waste water in another pipe for non -potable/ gardening/ toilet

(b)  whether measures taken to modernize the cottage industry are ineffective and if so, the

(c)  whether cottage industries in villages are gradually disappearing due to liberalization and if 
so, the details thereof and the criteria set for defining and reckoning cottage industries in villages;

liberal market forces along with the outcome thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
(SHRI BHANU PRATAP SINGH VERMA) 
 
(a): The ‘Cottage Industry’ has not been defined under the Khadi and Village Industries 
Commission Act, 1956. However, the broad contours of ‘Cottage Industry’ are covered under the 
‘Village Industry’ vertical under the purview of the Khadi and Village Industries Commission 
(KVIC) and are broadly classified under six groups for the purpose of implementation of its 
programmes which are as follows:  
1. Agro Based & Food Processing Industry (ABFPI) 
2. Mineral Based Industry (MBI) 
3. Wellness & Cosmetics Industry 
4. Handmade Paper, Leather & Plastic Industry (HPLPI)  
5. Rural Engineering and New Technology Industry (RENTI) 
6. Service Industry  
 
Ministry of MSME is implementing PMEGP scheme, a credit-linked subsidy programme 
since 2008-09 with KVIC as nodal agency at the national level for generating self-employment 
opportunities through establishment of micro enterprises, including village industries, throughout 
the country. 
 
Entrepreneurs Development Programme (EDP) training is imparted to beneficiaries who 
have established new micro enterprises under PMEGP, through KVIC, Khadi and Village 
Industries Boards (KVIBs) Training Centers as well as Accredited Training Centers run by Central 
Government, National Small Industries Corporation Limited (NSIC), National Institute for 
Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development (NIESBUD), National Institute for Micro, 
Small and Medium Enterprises (NIMSME), Indian Institute of Entrepreneurship (IIE), and their 
partner institutions under the administrative control of Ministry of MSME. State Governments, 
Banks, Rural Development and Self Employment Training Institutes (RUDSETI) reputed NGOs, 
and other organizations/institutions, identified by the Government from time to time also impart 
such training.

INITIATIVES UNDER THE ATMANIRBHAR BHARAT PACKAGE 
 
906.  SHRI B. LINGAIAH YADAV: 
 
Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether most of the firms were aware about the initiatives under the ‘Atma Nirbhar 
Bharat’ package but only half of them found it to be of any help, if so, the details thereof and 
reasons therefor; 
(b) whether given the lack of demand and business uncertainties, many firms did not find 
it rational to avail of financial assistance available under the Atmanirbhar Bharat package and 
also a majority of firms suggested that Government should have been more focused on 
creating a revival of demand for products and services; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof/corrective steps being taken by Government to help such 
MSMEs till date? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
(SHRI BHANU PRATAP SINGH VERMA) 
 
(a) to (c):  The Government has taken a number of recent initiatives under the Aatma 
Nirbhar Bharat Abhiyan to mitigate the negative impact of Covid-19 on small businesses  
including revival of demand for products and services in the country. Some of them are: 
 
i.  Credit Guarantee Scheme Subordinate Debt (CGSSD)for stressed MSMEs.  As on 
19.07.2022,  Rs. 90.47  Crore has been extended to 782 accounts under CGSSD. 
ii.   Guaranteed Emergency Credit Line (GECL) / Emergency Credit Line   Guarantee   
Scheme (ECLGS) for Businesses, including MSMEs. As on 30.06.2022, around 1.19 
crore businesses (including 1.13 crore MSMEs) have been provided collateral free 
loans amounting to Rs.3.48 lakh crore (Rs.2.32 lakh crore to MSMEs) under ECLGS 
scheme.  
iii.  Equity infusion through Self-Reliant India (SRI)Fund. SRI Fund has been 
operationalised, daughter funds are being empanelled and through them MSMEs are 
benefitting. 
iv.  New revised criteria of classification of MSMEs.  
v.    New registration of MSMEs through ‘Udyam Registration’ for Ease of Doing 
Business. As many 98,00,560 MSMEs with an employment of 7.46 crore have 
registered on the Udyam Portal. 
vi.  No global tenders for procurement up to Rs. 200 crores.

907.  SHRI BRIJLAL:  
 
Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government has launched a scheme called Raising and Accelerating MSMEs 
Performance (RAMP) to improve the performance of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises 
(MSMEs); 
(b) if so, the details thereof and the salient features of the said scheme; 
(c) whether the World Bank has provided financial assistance to India for this scheme 
and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) Government’s plans on opportunities to create employment in MSMEs through the 
RAMP scheme? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
(SHRI BHANU PRATAP SINGH VERMA) 
 
(a) & (b):  Yes, Sir. Government has launched a World Bank supported Central Sector 
Scheme called Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance (RAMP).  The scheme aims at 
strengthening institutions and governance at the Centre and State, improving Centre-State 
linkages and partnerships and improving access of MSMEs to market and credit, technology 
upgradation and addressing issues of delayed payments and greening of MSMEs. 
 
(c): RAMP programme 
will be implemented over a period of five years.  The total outlay 
for the scheme is  ₹6,062.45 crore or USD 808 M
illion, out of which ₹3750 crore or USD 500 
Million would be 
a loan from the World Bank and the remaining ₹2312.45 crore or USD 308 
Million would be funded by the Government of I
ndia (GoI). 
 
(d): Interventions under 
RAMP programme, by way of increasing access of MSMEs to 
market, technology and credit, increasing outreach to more MSMEs, inclusion of service 
sector, gender and greening initiatives etc., are aimed at increasing the performance of the 
MSME sector, thus resulting in more employment opportunities.

COST OF PRODUCTION FOR MSMEs 
 
909.   SHRI AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
 
 (a)   whether with the sharp rise in the cost of power, the overall cost of production for 
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) rose by 4 to 5 percent in the second half  
of April; 
 (b)     if so, the details thereof; 
 (c)   whether the cost of power soared to 12 to 13 rupees per unit in case of power 
backups, from the usual charge of 4 to 6 rupees; 
 (d)   whether absence of uninterrupted power will cost  SMEs  A 3000 to 3500  crore  in 
Jharkhand alone and if so, details of potential losses due to power crisis, State-wise; and 
 (e)      steps taken by Government to manage the power crisis? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
(SHRI BHANU PRATAP SINGH VERMA) 
(a) to (d):  The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) does not 
maintain the data in respect of cost of power. However, Ministry of Power informed that, 
the average rate for sale of power of Generating Stations has increased by about 5% in the 
quarter April-June 2022 as compared to quarter January-March 2022.  
              As reported by Government of Jharkhand, Jharkhand Bijli Vitran Nigam Limited 
(JBVNL) had purchased power from exchanges at higher rate up to 20 Rs per unit until 
capping of 12 Rs per unit by Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC). However, 
power is supplied to consumer at the tariff already approved by the Jharkhand State 
Electricity Regulatory Commission (JSERC). 
(e):        Ministry of Power has taken several steps to ensure smooth supply of coal to power 
plants for meeting power demand, which interalia includes constitution of Inter-Ministerial 
committee & Inter-Ministerial Sub Group to take various operational decisions. To enhance 
supply of coal to thermal power plants, the Ministry has been advised power plants to 
import about 61 MT coal for blending purposes during 2022-23.  JBVNL had executed 
Short term power purchase agreement with Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) to 
purchase 150 MW power on contingency basis.

910.   SHRI RAGHAV CHADHA:

(a)  the  Micro,  Small  and  Medium  Enterprises  (MSMEs) closed during the period from 2019 
to 2022 in the country;  
(b)  the number of MSMEs closed between 2016-2019;  
(c)  the  reasons  for  such  decrease  in  number  of  MSMEs units and whether Government has 
taken any steps to revive the MSMEs sector, particularly in Punjab and if so, the details thereof;  
(d)  the  details  of  credit  provided  to  MSMEs  through  the  banks  and NBFCs during the last 
three years; and  
(e)  whether  Government  proposes  to  facilitate  hassle  free  credit facility to MSMEs through 
banks and if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
(SHRI BHANU PRATAP SINGH VERMA) 
 
(a):   The number of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) closed during the period 
from 2019 to 2022, as per the erstwhile Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum and Udyam Registration 
data, are 9,667. 
 
(b):  The number of MSMEs closed between 2016-2019, as per the erstwhile Udyog Aadhaar 
Memorandum data, are 400.  
 
(c):  National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC) under Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium 
Enterprises (MSMEs) had conducted a study during August, 2020 with a sample size of 5,774 
MSMEs, across 32 States/UTs. It was found that 91% of MSMEs were functional and five most 
critical problems faced by MSMEs were identified as Liquidity (55% units), Fresh Orders (17% 
units), Labour (9% units), Logistics (12% units) and availability of Raw Material (8% units). 
 
          The Government of India, under Aatma Nirbhar Bharat, has announced measures to help 
micro, small and medium enterprises in the country, including Punjab. These include (i)  
Subordinate Debt for stressed MSMEs; (ii) Rs. 3 lakh crore Emergency Credit Line Guarantee 
Scheme (ECLGS) for bus
iness, including MSMEs, which has subsequently been increased to Rs. 5 
lakh crore; (iii) Rs. 50,000 crore equity infusion through Self-Reliant India Fund; (iv) New revised 
criteria of classification of MSMEs; (v) New registration of MSMEs through ‘Udyam Registration’ 
for Ease of Doing Business; (vi) No global tenders for procurement up to Rs. 200 crore.   
 
(d):  Credit provided to MSMEs, as per data provided by RBI, are at Annexure.  
 
(e): Government is facilitating hassle free credit facility to MSMEs through various schemes 
such as Emerge
ncy Credit Line Guarantee Scheme  (ECLGS) for business, including MSMEs; 
Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro & Small Enterprises, etc. being implemented through banks.

(NMET) as an autonomous body, if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; 
 
(b) the progress that has been made so far in this regard; and  
 
(c) whether Government has taken any other steps to boost mineral exploration in the 
country, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?

THE MINISTER OF MINES, COAL AND PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS

 (c): Ministry of Mines has taken the following steps to boost the mineral exploration in the

exploration agencies from National Mineral Exploration  Trust (NMET).  So far, nine 
agencies have been notified under the second proviso to Section 4(1) of the MMDR Act. 
2. Geological Survey of India  has given thrust on Pan -India mapping projects like National 
Geochemical Mapping, National Geophysical Mapping, National Aero -Geophysical 
Mapping and Specialized Thematic Mapping programmes which are expected to contribute 
immensely to delineate new potential areas for further systematic mineral exploration.

has been increased to 6.88 lakh sq.km for 18 minerals from a previous figure of 5.71 lakh 
sq.km for 10 minerals.

handed over to the concerned State Governments for auctioning as composite licence.

919.    DR. KANIMOZHI NVN SOMU: 
Will the Minister of MINES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government has taken any  steps to explore the development of lithium in the 
country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof along with the reserves of lithium in the country; 
(c) whether Government has recently signed an agreement with Argentina for joint exploration 
of lithium; 
(d)if so, the details thereof; 
(e) whether Government has entered into any other similar agreements with other countries for 
lithium sourcing; and 
(f) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF MINES, COAL AND PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
(SHRI PRALHAD JOSHI) 
 
(a) & (b):  Every year, as per approved annual Field Season Programme [FSP], Geological 
Survey of India [GSI], an attached office of Ministry of Mines, takes up different stages of 
mineral exploration viz. reconnaissance surveys (G4), preliminary exploratio n (G3) and 
general exploration (G2) following the guidelines of United Nations Framework Classification 
(UNFC) and Mineral Evidence and Mineral Content Rules (MEMC -2015) for augmenting 
mineral resource for various mineral commodities including lithium. 
During the last five years, GSI carried out 20 projects on Lithium and associated 
elements in Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Himachal Pradesh, 
Jharkhand, Jammu & Kashmir, Madhya Pradesh, Meghalaya, Rajasthan.    During the present 
FSP 2022-23, GSI has taken up 18 projects on Lithium in Arunachal Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, 
Jammu & Kashmir, Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Rajasthan. However, resource of 
lithium has not yet been augmented by GSI.  
Further, Atomic Minerals Directorate for Exploration and Research (AMD), a constituent unit 
of Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) is carrying out exploration for lithium in the potential 
geological domains of the country. Presently, AMD is carrying out exploration for lithium in 
parts of Mandya and Yadgir districts, Karnataka.  
(c) & (d): No, Sir. Khanij Bidesh India Ltd. (KABIL), a Joint Venture of three CPSEs under 
Ministry of Mines, has signed a Non -Binding Memorandum of Understanding [MoU] with 
three State-owned organizations of Argentina, for the p urpose of information sharing w.r.t. 
prospective mineral acreages of lithium: 
(e) &  (f): Yes , Sir . A G2G MoU has been signed between Government of India and the 
Government of Australia for co-operation in the field of mining and processing of Critical and 
Strategic Minerals such as Lithium. KABIL has signed a detailed MoU with Critical Minerals 
Facilitation Office [CMFO], Department of Industry, Science and Resources [DISER], 
Australia for identifying lithium and cobalt assets for joint investment decisions.

920. DR. FAUZIA KHAN: 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state :- 
(a) the details of works done for increasing use of bio ethanol/ biofuels in past five years, State-
 wise; 
(b) the details of funds allocated/released/spent for increasing use of bio ethanol/ biofuels for past 
three years, State-wise; 
(c) whether there is any delay in release of allocated funds; 
(d) if so, the reasons therefor; 
(e) the details of work done for increasing the use of bio ethanol/ biofuels in Maharashtra; 
(f) whether Government proposes to increase the allocation for Maharashtra for increasing the 
use of bio ethanol/ biofuels, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(g) whether there is any plan/proposal for increasing their use; and 
(h) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI RAMESWAR TELI) 
(a) to (e): Government had notified the National Policy on Biofuels – 2018 which laid down an 
indicative target of 20% blending of ethanol in petrol and 5% blending of biodiesel in diesel by 
2030 in the country. To promote the use of biofuels across the country including Maharashtra, 
various programmes such as Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme, wherein Oil Marketing 
Companies (OMCs) sell petrol blended with ethanol, Biodiesel blending programme wherein 
biodiesel is blended with diesel, Sustainable Alternative towards Affordable Transportation 
(SATAT) initiative wherein Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) is marketed along with Compressed 
Natural Gas (CNG) have been taken up.  
For biofuel production across the country including Maharashtra, the Government has taken steps 
on pricing, incentives, opened alternate route for ethanol production, notified Pradhan Mantri JI-
VAN Yojana for setting up 2 nd Generation (2G) ethanol bio-refineries based on agri residues for 
ethanol production, SATAT initiative for production of CBG and bio-manure from various waste/ 
biomass sources, notified interest subvention scheme for enhancement and expansion of ethanol 
distillation capacity etc.

2/2 
 
Financial assistance of Rs.150 crore each to the four commercial 2G ethanol projects at Bhatinda 
in Punjab, Panipat in Haryana, Bargarh in Odisha and Numaligarh in Assam and Rs.15 crore to

So far, Rs.151.50 crore has been released based on the milestones achieved as per the said 
Scheme.     
(f) to (h): States are free to produce biofuels as per production capacities. Further, entrepreneurs 
are free to set up biofuels plants anywhere in the country. For increasing the use of biofuels, a 
roadmap for Ethanol Blending in India 2020-25 was prepared by an inter-Ministerial Committee 
and placed in public domain on World Environment Day i.e. on 5 th June, 2021. This roadmap 
provides guidance to achieve the target of 20% ethanol blending in petrol by bringing all 
stakeholders together. Further, the National Policy on Biofuels -2018 has been amended recently. 
The amendments inter-alia include: 
i) allowing more feedstocks for production of biofuels, 
ii) advancing the ethanol blending target of 20% blending of ethanol in petrol to ESY 2025-
26 from 2030, 
iii) promotion of the production of biofuels in the country, under the Make in  India program, 
by units located in Special Economic Zones (SEZ)/ Export  Oriented Units (EoUs), and 
iv) grant of permission for export of biofuels in specific cases.

BOP system in energy sector 
 
 
937. Shri K.R.N. Rajeshkumar: 
 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government has established laws, rules and procedure for Blowout Prevention 
(BOP) system in energy sector in the country and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of implementation, compliance, penalties, and punishments related to BOP 
system; and 
(c) the details of number and frequency of security checks for prevention of blowout 
incidents and steps taken by Government to ensure enforceability? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS 
  (SHRI RAMESWAR TELI) 
 
(a): Blow out Prevention (BOP) system is covered under rule 146 and 158 of 
Petroleum and Natural Gas (Safety in Offshore Operations) Rules 2008 under 
the Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Act 1948. For onshore operations, 
BOP system is covered under regulations 52 to 58 of Oil Mines Regulations 
(OMR) 2017 developed under Mines Act 1952. The safe operations of BOP 
system shall be in accordance to Oil Industry Safety Directorate (OISD) 
Recommended Practices 174 (OISD-RP-174). 
(b): Oil Industry Safety Directorate is competent authority for implementation of 
the Petroleum and Natural Gas (Safety in Offshore Operations) Rules 2008 for 
offshore locations. Directorate General of Mines Safety (DGMS) is a regulator for 
onshore operations and it carries out inspection for implementation of Oil Mines 
Regulations (OMR) 2017. Implementation and compliance to the rules are 
monitored through internal audits by concerned organization, External Safety 
Audit by OISD and inspection by DGMS. Rule 173 of Petroleum and Natural Gas 
(Safety in Offshore Operations) Rules 2008 provides for punishment in 
accordance with the relevant provision of the Act in case of contravention of 
Rules. 
378

(c): Regulation # 56 of Oil Mines Regulations (OMR) 2017 and Rule 158 of 
P&NG Rules 2008 provides for the function and pressure testing of BOP. As per 
OISD-RP-174, major inspection of BOP including control system is carried out 
after every 5 years. For emergency preparedness, weekly mock BOP drill is 
carried out. During the audits OISD verifies the various requirements related to 
BOP and its control system.

DEMAND TO INCREASE CNG AND PNG INFRASTRUCTURE 
  
938.  SHRI SANJAY RAUT: 
  
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether Government proposes to increase the present level of gas share in the country’s fuel 
basket; 
(b) if so, the details thereof along with the steps taken/being taken by Government to bring the 
gas share at par with the world average; 
(c) whether Government has failed to achieve the target of providing PNG connection to 
households in the country and if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; and 
(d) the number of CNG/PNG stations proposed to be established in the rural and backward areas 
and time by when these stations are likely to be operationalized in the country? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
 
(SHRI RAMESWAR TELI) 
 
  
(a) and (b): Yes, Sir. The Government has set a target to raise the share of natural gas in energy 
mix to 15% in 2030 from about 6.3% now. To achieve the target, various initiatives have been 
taken which inter alia include the following:- 
i). Expansion of National Gas Grid to about 33,500 Km from current 21,715 Km. 
ii). Expansion of City Gas Distribution (CGD) network  
iii). Setting up of Liquefied Natural Gas Terminals. 
iv). Allocation of domestic gas to Compressed Natural Gas (Transport) / Piped Natural 
Gas (Domestic) in no cut category. 
v). Allowing marketing and pricing freedom to gas produced from high pressure/high 
temperature areas, deep water & ultra-deep water and from coal seams. 
vi). Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation (SATAT) initiatives to 
promote Bio-CNG. 
 
(c) and (d) Providing Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connections and establishment of Compressed 
Natural Gas (CNG) stations is part of the development of CGD network and the same is carried 
out by the entities authorized by Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB).  The 
CNG Stations and PNG connections are being provided by authorized entities as per timelines 
prescribed by PNGRB from time to time.  As on 31.05.2022, total 95.21 lakh PNG (Domestic) 
connections have been provided and 4531 CNG (Transport) stations have been established by the 
authorized entities. After completion of 11A city gas distribution (CGD) round, 295 
Geographical Areas (GAs) have been authorized which inter alia covers 98% of India’s 
population and 88% of its GAs.  As per Minimum Work Programme, CGD entities authorized 
upto 11A round, have to provide 12.33 crore PNG connections and establish 17,700 CNG 
stations by 2030 including in rural and urban areas.

provide for about 9.5 days of crude oil requirement.  In addition, Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) 
in the country have storage facilities for crude oil and petroleum products for 64.5 days.Hence, 
current total national capacity for storage of crude oil and petroleum products currently is 74 days.   
Levels of holding of reserves of crude and petroleum products are dynamic in nature and vary due to 
a number of factors such as timing of supplies and releases, product slate, seasonality, refinery 
shutdowns, committed transactions etc. 
(d)&(e) In July 2021, Government had approved the establishment of two additional commercial-
cum-strategic facilities with total storage capacity of 6.5 MMT at Chandikhol (4 MMT) and Padur 
(2.5 MMT), on a Public Private Partnership (PPP) mode.Government and OMCs evaluate, from time 
to time,the possibility of augmentation of storage capacities based on technical and commercial 
feasibility.

942 # Smt. KantaKardam:  
 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether Government proposes to allocate City Gas Distribution (CGD) network to all 
smart cities of the country; 
(b) if so, the time limit set for the same; 
(c) the details of households having Petroleum Natural Gas (PNG) connections and the 
details of the stipulated timeline for the purpose along with the proposed expansion of PNG 
connections in Uttar Pradesh; 
(d) whether some Ujjwala beneficiaries are also getting PNG connections in lieu of LPG 
cylinders; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
 
(SHRI RAMESWAR TELI) 
 
  
(a) and (b): Providing PNG domestic connections and establishment of CNG stations is part of 
development of City Gas Distribution (CGD) Networks and the same is being carried out by the 
entities authorized by Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB).  After completion 
of 11 A CGD Bidding round, 295 Geographical Areas (GAs) covering about 98% of the 
population and 88% of total geographical area of the Country spread over around 630 districts in 
28 states/UTs, including Smart Cities situated within the GAs, have been covered under the CGD 
network. Authorized entities will provide PNG domestic connections and install CNG stations as 
per Minimum Work Plan (MWP). 
(c) As on 31.05.2022, these CGD entities have provided 12,13,741 PNG domestic connections 
against MWP in Uttar Pradesh. PNGRB has authorized 41 GAs to various CGD entities for 
development of CGD Networks in Uttar Pradesh, which covers entire UP. 
(d) & (e) Governments provides deposit free LPG connections to women from poor households 
under PradhanMantriUjjwalaYojana(PMUY). There is no provision to provide a PNG 
connection in lieu of LPG connection under PMUY.

BIHAR AS DESTINATION OF ETHANOL PRODUCTION 
 
949. SHRI SUSHIL KUMAR MODI 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state :- 
(a) whether it is a fact that Bihar has abundant water, maize, broken rice and cheap labour which 
makes it a top destination for ethanol production; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that Initial positive intent was shown by 152 units with the intended 
capacity of 23,000 Kilo Litre Per Day (KLPD); 
(c) whether OMCs have issued long term off take agreements to only 17 units with the approved 
capacity of 1,080 KLPD which is only 5 per cent of initial intention; and 
(d) whether Government will increase the present quota from 36 crore litre/annum to 72 crore 
litre immediately? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS 
  
(SHRI RAMESWAR TELI) 
 
(a) to (d): Expression of Interest (EoI) for signing long term off take/bipartite agreement with 
upcoming dedicated ethanol plants in ethanol deficit States including Bihar for supply of 
denatured anhydrous ethanol was floated by Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) in August, 2021. 
The total estimated annual requirement of Bihar based on E20 scenario (i.e. blending 20% of 
ethanol in petrol) in 2025-26 is approximately 30.7 crore litres. After considering the annual 
availability from existing ethanol plants, a deficit requirement of 18.5 crore litres per annum was 
published in the EoI. 
In response to the EoI, 29 project proponents applied for the State of Bihar with a design capacity 
of 5600 Kilo litres per day/approximately 182.85 crore litre per annum.    
Long Term Offtake Agreements (LTOA) were signed during January, 2022 with 17 project 
proponents from Bihar with annual off take quantity of 34.62 crore litres which is already higher 
than the annual requirement of 18.5 crore litres published in the EoI.

(a) to (d): As per the ranking given by the respective publishing agencies, India’s ranking in 
Human Development Index (HDI) has moved from 130 among 189 countries in 2017 to 131 
among 189 countries in 2019, Global Hunger Index( GHI) has moved from 100 among 119 
countries in 2017 to 101 among 116 countries in 2021, Corruption Perception Index (CPI) has

methodologies, some of which are often questionable on many grounds. Many publishing 
agencies are using open source data or perception -based data which do not reflect India’s 
position in true sense. The Government has been engaging with publishing agencies and has, 
in several cases, highlighted significant issues in data quality and methodologies to them.

(ख) चेन्नई में ि ू सरे हवाई अड्े क े  दनमााण क े  दलए उपयुक्त स्थल क े  चयन हेतु पन्नूर और पराोंि ू र में अवरोि

स्‍ पाइसजेट‍क े ‍विमान‍को‍आपातकाल‍में‍उतारा‍जाना  
 
क्या नागर‍विमानन‍मंत्री यह बताने की क ृपा करेंगे कक :  
 
(क)  क्या यह सच है कक 5 जुलाई 2022 को दिल्ली से िुबई जा रहे स्पाइसजेट के विमान को  
पाककस्तान के कराची में इमरजेंसी लैंड ंग करानी पडी ; और  
(ख )  यदि हां , तो तत्संबंधी ब्यौरा क्या है ? 
उत्तर 
 
नागर‍विमानन‍मंत्रालय‍में‍राज्य‍मंत्री‍(जनरल‍(डा.)‍विजय‍कु मार‍ससंह‍(सेिाननि ृत्त)) 
 
 
(क) और (ि) दिनांक 05.07.2022 को , दिल्ली से िुबई जा रही िीटी -एमएक्सजी पंजीकरण-धारक 
मैससस स्पाइसजेट बी737-8 मैक्स, कॉकवपट क्रू ने यह िेिा कक ईंधन असंत ुलन चेतािनी प्राप्त 
होने के उपरांत ईंधन की मात्रा असामान्य रूप से कम होने लगी।  
 
कॉकवपट क्रू ने इस घटना के ललए असामान्य जांच स ूची (चेकललस्ट) की मिि ली तथा ईंधन 
ररसाि का संिेह करते ह ुए, विमान को कराची  ाइिटस करने का ननणसय ललया।  केबबन क्रू ने 
आपात की घोषणा नहीं की।  लैंड ंग  के उपरांत , कराची में की गई जाचं और ननरीक्षण में ईंधन 
ररसाि नहीं पाया गया।

उड़ान योजऩा के अंतर्गत र्ैर-प्रच़ालनरत म़ार्ग 
क्या ऩार्र विम़ानन मंत्री यह बताने की क ृपा करेंगे कक :  
 
(क )  सरकार की महत्िाकांक्षी उडान पररयोजना की क्षेत्रीय सम्पकक योजना के अंतगकत ननधि 
के क ुल आिंटन और उपयोधगता का राज्य चार , पररयोजना - बार ब्यौरा क्या है;  
(ि )  उडान पहल के अंतगकत क्षेत्रीय सम्पकक योजना के अंतगकत राज्य - बार ककतने मागक 
उपलब्ि कराए गए हैं;  
(ग)  इस योजना के अंतगकत दिए गए क ुल मागों में से स्थायी प्रचालन मागक ककतने हैं , 
तत्संबंिी राज्यिार ब्यौरा क्या है ; 
(घ)  क्या यह सच है कक उडान की क्षेत्रीय सम्पकक योजना के अंतगकत दिए गए मागों में से 
केिल 50  प्रनतशत ही स्थायी रूप से प्रचालन योग्य हैं, यदि हां , तो तत्संबंिी ब्यौरा क्या 
है; और  
(ङ) सरकार की दिए गए सभी मागों को कब तक प्रचालन योग्य बनाने की योजना है ? 
 
उत्तर 
 
ऩार्र विम़ानन मंत्ऱालय में ऱाज्य मंत्री (जनरल (ड़ा.) विजय कुम़ार ससंह (सेि़ाननिृत्त)) 
 
(क): नागर  विमानन मंत्रालय ने , िेश में अपररचाललत  और अल्प-पररचाललत  हिाईअड्डों से क्षेत्रीय 
हिाई संपकक बढाने और  जनता के ललए  हिाई यात्रा को ककफायती बनाने के  उद्िेश्य 
से, दिनांक  21-10-2016 को क्षेत्रीय संपकक योजना (आरसीएस)-उडान (उडे िेश का आम नागररक) 
शुरू की है।  उडान  एक बाजार  आिाररत  और स्ि-वित्तपोवित योजना है। इच्छ ुक 
एयरलाइनें , विलशष्ट मागों पर मांग के अपने आकलन के आिार पर उडान के तहत बोली के 
समय अपने प्रस्ताि प्रस्तुत करती हैं। योजना िस्तािेज के प्राििानों के अन ु
सार
, उडान 
के  अंतगकत उडानों के प्रचालन हेत ु, चयननत एयरलाइन  प्रचालकों (एसएओ) को  व्यिहायकता अंतर 
ननधियन  (िीजीएफ) प्रिान ककया जाता  है। ट्रंक मागों पर, कुछ छूटों के साथ , उडानों के प्रत्येक 
प्रस्थान पर 5000/- रुपये  का करारोपण करके , िीजीएफ जुटाया जाता है और योजना िस्तािेज के

आयुध लनमााणियों का लनगमीकरि  
 
841. डा. ककरोड़ी लाल मीिा  : 
 
 क्या रक्षा मंत्री यह बताने की कृपा करेंगे कक : 
 
(क ) राजस्थान सकहत देश में आयुध लनमााणियों की संख्या ककतनी है और तत्संबंधी राज्य-िार 
ब्यौरा क्या है ;  
(ख) क्या सरकार ने आयुध लनमााणियों का लनगमीकरि करने का लनिाय ललया है ;  
(ग) क्या इन 41 आयुध लनमााणियों को सात लनगमों में पररिलतात करने का प्रस्ताि है ; 
(घ) यकद हां, तो तत्संबंधी ब्यौरा क्या है और यकद नह़ीं, तो इसक े  क्या कारि हैं ; 
(ड.) इस संबंध में कमाचाररयों/यूलनयनों/फ े डरेशनों/संगठनों की क्या प्रलतकिया है ; 
(च) क्या सरकार ने देश की सुरक्षा और रक्षा तैयाररयों  और उक्त कारखानों में कायारत 
कमाचाररयों क े  कहतों क े  बारे में कोई अध्ययन ककया है ; और  
(छ) यकद हां, तो इससे क्या प्रभाि पडेगा, तत्संबंधी ब्यौरा क्या है ? 
 
उत्तर 
रक्षा मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री अजय भट्ट) 
(क):  देश में 41 आयुध लनमााणियां है । तथावप, राजस्थान राज्य में कोई आयुध लनमाािी नह़ीं 
है । राज्य-िार सूची अनुबंध-क  क े  रूप में संलग्न है । 
(ख) से (घ) : क ें द्ऱीय मंवत्रमंडल क े  कदनांक 16 जून, 2021 क े  लनिाय क े  अनुसरि में आयुध 
लनमााणियों में प्रकायाात्मक स्िायत्तता, कुशलता और निीन विकास क्षमता और निाचार क े  
प्रितान हेतु आयुध लनमाािी बोडा की उत्पादन इकाइयों को रक्षा क्षेत्र क े  7 सािाजलनक उपिमों 
(पूिा रूप से भारत सरकार द्वारा स्िालमत्ि) क े  साथ 41 इकाइयों में कदनांक 1 अक्तूबर, 2021 
(''लनयत ताऱीख'') से पररिलतात कर कदया गया है, णजनक े  नाम ( i) म्यूलनशंस इंकडया लललमटेड 
(ii) आमाडा व्ह़ीकल्स लनगम लललमटेड ( iii) एडिान्सस्ड िेपन्सस एंड इणक्िपमेंट इंकडया लललमटेड (iv) 
ट्रूप कम्फट्सा लललमटेड ( v) यंत्र इंकडया लललमटेड ( vi) इंकडया ऑप्टेल लललमटेड और ( vii) 
ग्लाइडसा इंकडया लललमटेड हैं । वििरि अनुबंध-ख क े  रूप में संलग्न है । 
613

(ड.): पूिािती आयुध लनमाािी बोडा क े  कमाचाररयों क े कई फ े डरेशनों, संगठनों एिं संघों ने आयुध 
लनमाािी बोडा क े  लनगमीकरि करने क े  सरकार क े  लनिाय क े  विरुद्ध अभ्यािेदन कदया है । 
(च) और (छ): विभाग ने मैससा  क े पीएमजी एडिाइजऱी सविासेस प्राइिेट लललमटेड (प्रमुख 
कंसोकटायम सदस्य) सकहत अन्सय कंसोकटायम सदस्य क े  रूप में मैससा खैतान एंड कंपनी लललमटेड 
को  परामशादायी एजेंसी क े  रूप में आयुध लनमाािी बोडा क े  मानि संसाधन से संबंलधत मामलों 
सकहत लनगमीकरि की प्रकिया में विभाग की सहायता क े  ललए सामररक और कायाान्सियन प्रबंधन 
परामशादायी सेिाएं प्रदान करने हेतु चयलनत ककया है । सरकार ने आयुध लनमाािी बोडा 
(ओएफबी) क े  कमाचाररयों और कामगारों क े  कहतों को सुरणक्षत करने क े  ललए लनम्नललणखत कदम 
उठाए हैं :   
(i) उत्पादन यूलनटों और लचणन्सहत गैर-उत्पादन इकायों से भी संबंलधत ओएफबी क े  सभी 
कमाचाररयों (समूह क, ख एिं ग) को लनयुवक्त  की  ताऱीख से दो िर्ा की अिलध क े  ललए वबना 
प्रलतलनयुवक्त भत्ते (मालनत प्रलतलनयुवक्त) क े  विदेश सेिा की तजा पर नए ड़ीपीएसयू क े  ललए 
सामूकहक रूप से स्थानांतरि कर कदया गया ।  
(ii) कमाचाररयों क े  नए ड़ीपीएसयू में प्रलतलनयुवक्त पर रहने तक िे अपने  िेतनमान, भत्तों, 
अिकाश,  लचककत्सा  सुविधाएं, कैररयर में प्रोन्सनलत और अन्सय सेिा शतों सकहत क े न्सद्र सरकार क े 
का लमाकों पर लागू मौजूदा लनयमों , विलनयमों और आदेशों क े  अध्यधीन रहेंगे । 
(iii) ओएफबी मुख्यालय (कोलकाता), ओएफबी नई कदल्ली कायाालय,  ओएफबी क े स्कूलों और 
अस्पतालों से संबंलधत ओएफबी क े  सभी कमाचाररयों (समूह क, ख और ग) का लनयत  ताऱीख से 
प्रारंभ में दो िर्ा की अिलध क े  ललए रक्षा उत्पादन विभाग क े  तहत आयुध लनमाािी (समन्सिय 
और सेिा) में सामूकहक रूप से स्थानांतरि ककया गया है ।  
(iv) सेिालनिृत्त होने िाले और मौजूदा कमाचाररयों की पेंशन देनदाररयां सरकार  द्वारा िहन की 
जाएगी । कदनांक  01.01.2004 क े  पश्चात लनयुक्त कमाचाररयों क े  ललए क े न्सद्र सरकार क े  कमाचाररयों 
क े  ललए लागू राष्ट्रीय पेंशन योजना लागू है और इसे ड़ीपीएसयू द्वारा अपना ललया गया है, णजसमें 
राष्ट्रीय पेंशन प्रिाली क े  तहत क े न्सद्र सरकार क े  कमाचाररयों पर लागू सभी विशेर् प्रािधान जाऱी 
रहेंगे ।

954. श्री ए.ए. रहीम:  
 
क्या साांख्यिकी और कार्यक्रम कार्ायन्वर्न मांत्री र्ह बताने की क ृ पा करेंगे लक:  
 
(क) लिगत िर्य में मालसक उपभोक्ता मूल्य सूचकाांक आधाररत मुद्रास्फीलत सांबांधी आांकडो का राज्य-
िार राष्ट्र ीर् औसत क्या है; 
(ख) उच्च राष्ट्र ीर् औसत क े  क्या कारण हैं; और  
(ग) सरकार द्वारा इसे रोकने क े  ललए क्या उपार् लकए गए हैं?  
 
उत्तर 
 
साांख्यिकी और कार्यक्रम कार्ायन्वर्न राज्य मांत्री (स्वतांत्र प्रभार), र्ोजना मांत्रालर् राज्य मांत्री (स्वतांत्र प्रभार) 
तथा कॉपोरेट कार्य मांत्रालर् राज् र् मांत्री [राि इांद्रजीत लसांह]  
 
(क) साांख्यिकी और कार्यक्रम कार्ायन्वर्न मांत्रालर् देश क े  लिए आधार 2012=100 क े  साथ मालसक अखिि 
भारतीय उपभोक्ता मूल्य सूचकाांक (सीपीआई) और उस पर आधाररत मुद्रास्फीलत दरें जारी क रता है । जुिाई 
2021 से जून 2022 (अनांलतम) की अवलध क े  दौरान अखिि भारतीय सीपीआई (सांयुक्त) पर आधाररत मालसक 
राज्य-वार और अखिि भारतीय सामान्य मुद्रास्फीलत दर अनुबांध-1 में दी गई है । 
 
(ख) और ( ग) सीपीआई आधाररत मुद्रास्फीलत में समग्र वृखि िैलिध्यपूणय है और  इसका प्रमुि कारण खाद्य 
और ई ांधन सांबांधी सूचकाांक में बढोत्तरी है। हाि क े  महीनोां में मुद्रास्फीलत में अलधकाांशत: वृखि का एक  प्रमुख 
कारण  यूरोप में युि से जुडे आपूलति ढाांचे को उत्तरदार्ी ठहराया जा सकता है।  
प्रमुि आवश्यक वस्तुओां की मूल्य खथथलत की सरकार द्वारा लनयलमत रूप से लनगरानी की जाती है और समय -
समय पर सुधारात्मक कारिवाई की जाती है। मुद्रास्फीलत को लनर्ांलत्रत करने क े  लिए सरकार द्वारा  आपूलति 
सांबांधी अनेक उपाय लकए गए हैं। इनमें दािोां पर आयात शुल्क और उपकर में कमी, टैररफ का युखक्तकरण 
और िाद्य तेिोां और लतिहनोां पर स्टॉक सीमा िागू करना, प्याज और दािोां क े  लिए बफर स्टॉक का 
रिरिाव,  30 जून, 2022 तक आिश्यक िस्तु अलधलनर्म, 1955 की अनुसूची में एक आिश्यक िस्तु क े  
रूप में सोर्ा भोजन का समािेशन ओर 30 जून, 2022 तक सोर्ा भोजन पर स्टॉक सीमा का अलधरोपण 
शालमल है । इसक े  अिावा, सरकार द्वारा मूल्य खथथरीकरण क े  लिए दािोां और प्याज का बफर स्टॉक व्यिख्यथथत 
रिा गया है । बाजार में कीमतोां को कम करने क े  लिए बफर स्टॉक से दािोां और प्याज को अांशशोलधत मात्रा 
में लनकालना शुरू कर लदर्ा गर्ा है। अरहर और उडद क े  आयात को 31.03.2023 तक ' लन:शुल्क श्रेणी' क े  
तहत रिा गया है। मसूर क े  सांबांध में, मूि आयात शुल्क और क ृ लि अवसांरचना और लवकास उपकर को 
शून्य पर िाया गया है।

ii. स्वदेशी रूप से उत्पन्न होने वाले स्िैप की उपलब्धता बढ़ाने के भलए इस्पात स्िैप प ुनचतिण
नीनत को अधधस ूधचत करना।
iii. गैर-मानकीक ृत इस्पात के ववननमातण तथा आयात को रोकने के भलए इस्पात ग ुणवत्ता
नन यंत्रण आदेश जारी करना।
iv. इस्पात आयातों के अधिम पंजीकरण के भलए इस्पात आयात ननगरानी प्रणाली
(एसआईएमएस)।
v. पूाँजीगत ननवेश को आकवर्तत करके घरेल ू उपयोग और ननयातत के भलए देश में ही ववशेर्
इस्पात के ववननमातण को बढ़ावा देने के भलए 6, 322 करोड़ रुपये के पररव्यय के साथ ववशेर्
इस्पात हेतु उत्पादन संबद्ध प्रोत्साहन (पीएलआई) योजना को अधधस ूधचत करना।

(ग) और (घ): तनयाषत में बढोत्तरी के साथ वपछले क ुछ िर्षों के दौरान तैयार इस्पात के उत्पादन और 
खपत में ि ृवि हुई है, र्जससे घरेलू इस्पात उद्योग पर सकारात्मक प्रिाि पडा है। वित्त िर्षष 2020-21 
के दौरान म ुख्यतया कोविड -19 महामारी जतनत व्यिधानों के कारण इस्पात के उत्पादन में कमी दजष की 
गई थी। सरकार ने उत्पादन को बढाने और देश में घरेल ू इस्पात उद्योग के दहतों की रक्षा करने के भलए 
तनम्नभलखखत कदम उठाए हैं: - 
(i) राष्ट्रीय इस्पात नीतत 2017 र्जसमें रणनीततक अन ुप्रयोगों के भलए इस्पात और हाई -ग्रेड 
ऑटोमोदटि स्टील, विद्युत ् इस्पात , विशेर्ष इस्पात एिं भमश्र-धात ु की समग्र मांग को घरेल ू स्तर 
पर पूरा करने की पररकल्पना की गई है , को अधधस ूधचत करना।   
(ii) सरकारी एजेंभसयों द्िारा मेड इन इंडडया इस्पात की अधधप्रार्तत को बढािा देने हेत ु घरेलू रूप से 
वितनभमषत लौह एिं इस्पात उत्पाद (डीएमआई एंड एसपी ) नीतत।  
(iii) इस्पात आयातों के अधग्रम पंजीकरण हेत ु इस्पात आयात तनगरानी प्रणाली (एसआईएमएस) की 
अधधस ूचना। 
(iv) केन्रीय बजट 2021 -22 में गैर-भमश्र धात ु, भमश्र धात ु और स्टेनलेस स्टील के सेमीज , फ्लैट एिं 
लॉन्ग उत्पादों पर सीमा श ुल्क को एक समान रूप से घटाकर 7.5 % कर ददया गया है। केन्रीय 
बजट 2022-23 में, इस्पात स्क्रैप पर म ूल सीमा शुल्क (बीसीडी) में ददनांक 31.03.2023 तक 
छूट प्रदान की गई है और इस्पात उत्पादों पर पाटनरोधी श ुल्क (एडीडी ) और प्रततकारी श ुल्क 
(सीिीडी) को िी हटा ददया गया है।  
(v) सरकार ने ददनांक 21.05.2022 की अधधस ूचना द्िारा इस्पात के कच्चे माल और इस्पात उत्पादों 
के  शुल्कों में संशोधन ककए हैं , र्जसमें एंथ्रेसाइट/पल्िेराइज्ड कोल इंजेक्शन (पीसीआई ) कोल , कोक 
और सेमी कोक तथा फ े रो -तनकेल पर आयात श ुल्क को घटाकर श ून्य कर ददया गया है। लौह 
अयस्क/सान्र और लौह अयस्क पैलेट पर तनयाषत श ुल्क को बढाकर क्रमशः 50% और 45% कर 
ददया गया है और कई इस्पात उत्पादों पर 15% तनयाषत श ुल्क लगाया गया है।
